title: How Transformers Compute Self-Attention
youtubeTitle: How Transformers Compute Attention in Parallel ⚡ #Shorts
youtubeDescription: Understand how the Transformer architecture computes Multi-Head Self-Attention using Query, Key, and Value vectors to process all tokens in parallel.

scenes.visualBody: Processing tokens sequentially forces every word to wait for the previous hidden state, destroying parallel training.
scenes.voiceText: Before Transformers, sequential networks processed tokens one by one, creating a massive training bottleneck.
scenes.source: Vaswani et al., Attention Is All You Need (2017)

scenes.visualBody: Tokens project into Query, Key, and Value vectors, computing all-to-all attention scores simultaneously in parallel.
scenes.voiceText: Self-attention projects tokens into Query, Key, and Value vectors, computing all-to-all relationships in parallel.
scenes.source: Vaswani et al., Attention Is All You Need

scenes.visualBody: Multi-head attention combines with feed-forward sublayers, stabilized by residual streams and LayerNorm.
scenes.voiceText: Each block fuses multi-head attention with a feed-forward layer, linked by residual connections to prevent vanishing gradients.

scenes.visualBody: Native attention scales at O(N squared) memory; production engines use FlashAttention and KV caching to sustain long contexts.
scenes.voiceText: Because full attention scales quadratically, production models use FlashAttention and KV caching to unlock massive context windows.
scenes.source: Dao et al., FlashAttention & vLLM Architectures
